quizzes.question: You are at the bar and want to ask what tapas they have. Which one is right?
quizzes.takeaway: Addressing a business is almost always plural in Spain.

quizzes.question: You want the set lunch. You say “Sí, el del día, por favor.” What is missing?
quizzes.answer: menú — “Sí, el menú del día, por favor.”
quizzes.takeaway: You will be understood without it. You will also sound like you are guessing.

quizzes.question: You want to ask if they know where the nearest health centre is. Saber or conocer?
options: ¿Conoce dónde está el centro de salud?
¿Sabe dónde está el centro de salud?
quizzes.answer: ¿Sabe dónde está el centro de salud?
quizzes.takeaway: Saber = information. Conocer = familiarity.

quizzes.place: the queue at your local ayuntamiento
quizzes.question: You turn up at the town hall to register. The first thing they ask is whether you have one of these. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Learn “cita previa” before you learn anything else. You will need it for the NIE, the padrón and the doctor.

quizzes.question: The officer asks “¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje?” You are moving here. What do you say?
quizzes.answer: Both are fine — “Vengo a vivir aquí” is what you will hear most.
quizzes.takeaway: Verb of motion + a + infinitive. “Vengo a…”, “Voy a…”, “Salgo a…”.

quizzes.place: the taxi rank outside the terminal
quizzes.question: You get in and want to give the driver an address. Which opener sounds native?
quizzes.takeaway: You llevar a person. You tomar a bus. The driver conduce.

quizzes.place: a bank branch on a Tuesday morning
quizzes.question: You want an everyday current account. What do you ask for?
quizzes.takeaway: Actual = present-day, not “actual”. One of the false friends that bites hardest.

quizzes.place: a phone shop on the high street
quizzes.question: You do not want to be locked in. How do you ask for a contract with no minimum term?
quizzes.takeaway: Sin permanencia = no lock-in. Sin contrato = prepaid. They are not the same offer.

quizzes.question: You have a headache and need to say so. Which is right?
quizzes.takeaway: Me duele + singular. Me duelen + plural. Never “estoy dolor”.

quizzes.place: an empty flat with the estate agent waiting
quizzes.question: The agent mentions the deposit you will have to put down. Which word is that?
quizzes.takeaway: Fianza = deposit. Aval = guarantee. Ask which one they want before you sign.

quizzes.question: You are thanking a neighbour for their help. Which one?
quizzes.takeaway: Por = the reason behind. Para = the goal ahead.

quizzes.place: a friend’s kitchen, making small talk
quizzes.question: You want to say you are bored right now. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Estoy aburrido = I am bored. Soy aburrido = I am boring. Pick carefully.

quizzes.place: a shop, having just knocked something over
quizzes.question: You did something clumsy and want to say you are embarrassed. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Embarazada = pregnant. Vergüenza = embarrassment.

quizzes.question: You have a blocked nose and a sore throat. What do you tell the pharmacist?
quizzes.answer: Estoy constipado. (constipada if you are female)
quizzes.takeaway: Estoy constipado = I have a cold. It is not what it looks like.

quizzes.place: a government office with a queue number
quizzes.question: Same afternoon, two places. Where would you use usted?
quizzes.takeaway: Default to tú in daily life. Save usted for the counter with a queue number.

quizzes.place: a bar terrace with two friends
quizzes.question: You are addressing two friends informally, in Spain. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: In Spain, vosotros for friends, ustedes for formality. Both exist.

quizzes.place: a bar, at the counter rather than a table
quizzes.question: You want a small draught beer. What do Spaniards actually say?
quizzes.takeaway: ¿Me pones…? at the bar. ¿Me pone…? if you are being formal.

quizzes.place: a restaurant, at the end of a long lunch
quizzes.question: You want the bill. Which is the natural one?
quizzes.takeaway: La cuenta = the bill. La factura = the invoice you claim on.

quizzes.place: a queue, filling in a form
quizzes.question: Someone asks for your address. Which question did they use?
quizzes.takeaway: Cuál asks which one. Qué asks what a thing means.

quizzes.question: It is 40 degrees. How do you say it is very hot?
quizzes.takeaway: Muy + adjective. Mucho + noun. Hace + weather.

quizzes.topic: A verb that changes by country
quizzes.question: In Spain, how do you say you are going to catch the bus?
quizzes.answer: Both work in Spain — coger is the everyday one.
quizzes.takeaway: In Spain: coger. Across the Atlantic: tomar. Know why they differ.

quizzes.place: the market, with a queue behind you
quizzes.question: You want half a kilo of tomatoes. Which?
options: ¿Me pone la mitad de kilo de tomates?
¿Me pone medio de kilo de tomates?
quizzes.takeaway: Medio kilo, media hora. La mitad de = half of that particular thing.

quizzes.question: They ask “¿Cómo lo quiere?” You want a little off, just the ends. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Las puntas, por detrás, por los lados. Three phrases, one survivable haircut.

quizzes.question: A neighbour steps into the lift. What do you say?
quizzes.takeaway: Say hello when you walk into a small space. Silence is the impolite option.

quizzes.place: a tapas bar, ordering for the table
quizzes.question: You like tapas — plural. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: The thing you like is the subject. Count it, then pick gusta or gustan.

quizzes.topic: A word that traps English speakers
quizzes.place: your new town, describing it to someone back home
quizzes.question: You want to say the people here are very friendly. Which?
options: La gente aquí son muy amables.
La gente aquí es muy amable.
Las gentes aquí son muy amables.
quizzes.answer: La gente aquí es muy amable.
quizzes.takeaway: La gente es. Not son. One of the last errors to disappear.

quizzes.question: You want your coffee to take away. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: ¿Para tomar aquí o para llevar? Learn the question, not just the answer.

quizzes.topic: A noun that looks like it broke
quizzes.place: a bar, ordering the simplest thing there is
quizzes.question: You want cold water. Which is correct?
quizzes.takeaway: El agua, but fría. The article changes; the gender does not.

quizzes.place: a bar, meeting someone for the first time
quizzes.question: You have lived here two months. Which?
options: Hace dos meses que vivo aquí.
Hace dos meses que viví aquí.
quizzes.answer: Hace dos meses que vivo aquí.
quizzes.takeaway: Hace dos meses que vivo aquí. Present tense, because you still live here.

quizzes.place: the doorway after your language class
quizzes.question: You want to suggest meeting a friend on Friday. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Quedar = meet up on purpose. Encontrarse = bump into. Reunirse = at work.

quizzes.place: a café, trying to explain your job
quizzes.question: English "conversation" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -tion → -ción, always feminine, always accented.

quizzes.question: English "university" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ty → -dad. Feminine, and no accent needed.

quizzes.question: How do you turn "rápido" into "rapidly"?
quizzes.takeaway: Feminine adjective + -mente. Keep the accent you started with.

quizzes.question: English "delicious" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ous → -oso. Then make it agree with what it describes.

quizzes.question: English "document" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ment → -mento. Except gobierno, which you will meet at the town hall.

quizzes.question: English "difference" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ence → -encia, feminine. Spanish rarely doubles consonants.

quizzes.question: Your dentist is a woman. What do you call her?
quizzes.takeaway: -ista never changes. Change the article instead.

quizzes.place: reading a sign on a public building
quizzes.question: English "public" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ic → -ico, accented on the third-from-last syllable.

quizzes.question: English "active" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ive → -ivo, then agree it.

quizzes.place: a bank, reading the small print
quizzes.question: English "necessary" becomes which Spanish word?
quizzes.takeaway: -ary → -ario. And Spanish almost never doubles a consonant.

quizzes.place: a theatre, looking for the way out
quizzes.question: You see a sign saying "ÉXITO". What does it mean?
quizzes.takeaway: Éxito = success. Salida = exit. Do not follow the wrong sign.

quizzes.question: You want to say a friend is sensible (level-headed). Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Sensible = sensitive. Sensato = sensible.

quizzes.question: You want to say "actually, I live in Valencia". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Actualmente = currently. En realidad = actually.

quizzes.place: a shop, holding up a shirt
quizzes.question: The shirt is too big. Which do you say?
quizzes.takeaway: Largo = long. Grande = big.

quizzes.question: Which word means "clothes"?
quizzes.takeaway: La ropa está — singular, always.

quizzes.question: The gestor asks for "la carpeta". What do they want?
quizzes.takeaway: Carpeta = folder. Alfombra = carpet.

quizzes.question: The notice says "se ruega asistir". What is being asked?
quizzes.takeaway: Asistir = attend. Ayudar = help.

quizzes.place: a form asking what you did
quizzes.question: You want to say "I realized I was wrong". Which?
options: Me di cuenta de que estaba equivocado.
quizzes.answer: Me di cuenta de que estaba equivocado.
quizzes.takeaway: Realizar = carry out. Darse cuenta de = realise.

quizzes.question: You want to say "sorry to bother you". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Molestar = to bother. Completely ordinary, use it freely.

quizzes.question: You want to call a situation embarrassing. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Situación embarazosa = fine. Estoy embarazada = a very different sentence.

quizzes.place: a phone shop, explaining a fault
quizzes.question: You want to say “the problem”. Which is correct?
quizzes.takeaway: El problema, el tema, el idioma. Greek words keep their gender.

quizzes.topic: A noun that breaks the rule
quizzes.question: You hurt your right hand and need to say so. Which is correct?
quizzes.takeaway: La mano, la foto, la moto. The -o is lying to you.

quizzes.topic: A noun that breaks it the other way
quizzes.place: wishing someone well in the morning
quizzes.question: It is nine in the morning and you pass a neighbour. Which greeting?
quizzes.takeaway: Buenos días, buenas tardes, buenas noches. Only the first is masculine.

quizzes.place: a market stall, praising the produce
quizzes.question: The oranges on the stall are delicious. Which is correct?
quizzes.takeaway: Noun sets the gender and number. Verb and adjective follow.

quizzes.question: You want to say "I am going to look for a flat". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Voy a + infinitive. Never leave out the a.

quizzes.question: You want to say "I have just arrived". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Acabo de + infinitive = I have just…

quizzes.question: You are asking whether there is a pharmacy nearby. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Hay = there is one somewhere. Está = where the known one is.

quizzes.question: You want to say you can drive. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Sé = I know how to. Puedo = I am able to right now.

quizzes.place: a bar, needing one more thing
quizzes.question: You want to ask for the bill. Which verb?
options: Voy a preguntar por la cuenta.
quizzes.takeaway: Pedir = request a thing. Preguntar = ask a question.

quizzes.question: They say "trae algo de postre". What are they asking?
quizzes.takeaway: Traer = towards me. Llevar = away from me.

quizzes.question: It is three o clock. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Es la una, but son las dos, las tres, las diez.

quizzes.question: You want to say "I get up at seven". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Me levanto, me ducho, me acuesto. Keep the pronoun.

quizzes.question: The natural way to say "I forgot the keys" is:
quizzes.takeaway: Se me olvidó / se me olvidaron. The object decides the verb.

quizzes.question: You ate at a new place earlier today. In Spain you would most likely say:
options: Hoy comí en un sitio nuevo.
Hoy he comido en un sitio nuevo.
Hoy como en un sitio nuevo.
quizzes.answer: Hoy he comido en un sitio nuevo.
quizzes.takeaway: Hoy / esta semana / este año → he + participle.

quizzes.place: texting a friend who is ill
quizzes.question: You want to say "I hope you are well". Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Espero que + subjunctive. Learn it as a phrase first, a rule later.

quizzes.question: A friend says "¿qué tal, tío?". What did they call you?
quizzes.takeaway: Tío = mate, between friends. Never at the counter.

quizzes.topic: The word you will hear most
quizzes.question: What does "vale" mean in everyday Spain?
quizzes.takeaway: Vale is the single most useful word in Spain. Use it liberally.

quizzes.question: A friend gets the flat they wanted. You say:
quizzes.takeaway: Guay = cool. Qué bien = great, and safe in any country.

quizzes.question: In Spain, what do you call a mobile phone?
quizzes.takeaway: Móvil and ordenador in Spain. Celular and computadora elsewhere.

quizzes.place: a café at nine in the morning
quizzes.question: You want orange juice in Madrid. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Zumo and patatas in Spain. Jugo and papas across the Atlantic.

quizzes.place: looking for somewhere to leave the car
quizzes.question: In Spain, how do you say "to park"?
quizzes.takeaway: Aparcar and conducir in Spain.

quizzes.place: a bar on a Friday evening
quizzes.question: A friend says "mañana curro". What are they doing tomorrow?
quizzes.takeaway: Curro = job, informally. Trabajo on the paperwork.

quizzes.place: a small shop with a brown and yellow sign
quizzes.question: Where do you buy stamps in Spain?
quizzes.takeaway: Sellos at the estanco. It is the errand nobody explains.

quizzes.question: Your tap is dripping. Which shop?
quizzes.takeaway: -ería = the shop for that thing. One ending, twenty shops.

quizzes.place: your local health centre, on the phone
quizzes.question: You want to book an appointment with your GP. Which?
options: Quiero pedir cita con mi médico de cabecera.
Quiero preguntar cita con mi médico principal.
Quiero una reserva con mi doctor.
quizzes.answer: Quiero pedir cita con mi médico de cabecera.
quizzes.takeaway: Pedir cita con el médico de cabecera. Three words that unlock the system.

quizzes.place: a notice in your building's hallway
quizzes.question: A notice announces "la junta de la comunidad". What is it?
quizzes.takeaway: La junta = the meeting. Attend one and your Spanish will age five years in a night.

quizzes.place: the bin area at ten at night
quizzes.question: Which bin does glass go in?
quizzes.takeaway: Verde glass, amarillo plastic, azul paper. Learn the colours, not the words.

quizzes.place: an empty flat with no power
quizzes.question: You need to set up an electricity contract. The phrase is:
quizzes.takeaway: Alta = switch on. Baja = switch off. Opposites, one letter apart in your memory.

quizzes.place: an office full of filing cabinets
quizzes.question: What does a "gestor" do for you?
quizzes.takeaway: Gestoría: the shortcut through Spanish bureaucracy. Budget for it.

quizzes.question: What does "autónomo" mean in Spain?
quizzes.takeaway: Autónomo = self-employed, and it costs a fixed monthly amount.

quizzes.question: How is "hola" pronounced?
quizzes.takeaway: Write the h. Never say it.

quizzes.question: How is the j in "trabajo" pronounced?
options: Like the ch in Scottish loch
quizzes.answer: Like the ch in Scottish loch
quizzes.takeaway: J always rasps. G rasps before e and i only.

quizzes.question: Which means "dog"?
quizzes.takeaway: Pero / perro, caro / carro. The trill carries meaning.

quizzes.place: ordering at a bar in Madrid
quizzes.question: In most of Spain, how is the c in "cerveza" pronounced?
quizzes.takeaway: Central and northern Spain: c and z are th. Nobody will misunderstand either way.

quizzes.topic: When the accent changes the word
quizzes.question: What is the difference between "papa" and "papá"?
quizzes.takeaway: The accent is not decoration. It is spelling.

quizzes.topic: The letter English does not have
quizzes.place: talking about how old you are
quizzes.question: What is the difference between "año" and "ano"?
options: One is a year, the other is not something you want to say
quizzes.answer: One is a year, the other is not something you want to say
quizzes.takeaway: Tengo treinta años. Always type the ñ.

quizzes.place: saying a word you have only read
quizzes.question: Where is the stress in "hablo" (no written accent)?
quizzes.takeaway: Vowel, n or s → stress the second-to-last. Otherwise the last.

quizzes.question: The stallholder says "son dos con cincuenta". How much?
quizzes.takeaway: Dos con cincuenta = 2,50 €. Comma for decimals, symbol at the end.

quizzes.question: A form is dated 04/09/2026. Which date is that?
quizzes.takeaway: Day, month, year. And months are lower-case.

quizzes.question: Your appointment says 16:30. What time is that?
quizzes.takeaway: 16:30 written, “las cuatro y media” spoken.

quizzes.question: Which sounds most natural at a busy bar in Spain?
options: Perdone, señor, ¿sería tan amable de ponerme una caña?
quizzes.takeaway: Short is not rude in Spain. Warm tone does the work.

quizzes.place: a shop where the assistant is your age
quizzes.question: Someone says "puedes tutearme". What are they offering?
options: Call me by my first name
quizzes.takeaway: If they offer tutearme, switch on the spot.

quizzes.question: You need to squeeze past someone. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Perdón to get past. Lo siento when you mean it.

quizzes.question: Someone thanks you. Which reply is most common in Spain?
quizzes.takeaway: De nada. Never bienvenido.

quizzes.topic: Saying you did not catch it
quizzes.question: You did not catch what someone said. The most useful phrase is:
quizzes.takeaway: Ask for slower, not for English. It is the whole difference.

quizzes.question: You need a word you do not know. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: ¿Cómo se dice…? and ¿Qué significa…? Two phrases, endless vocabulary.

quizzes.place: someone asks how your Spanish is
quizzes.question: Someone asks how your Spanish is going. A natural modest answer:
quizzes.takeaway: Más o menos for honest. Muy bien, never mucho bien.

quizzes.place: a call you have been putting off
quizzes.question: You answer the phone in Spain. What do you say?
quizzes.takeaway: ¿Dígame? to answer. And phone Spanish is hard for everyone.

quizzes.question: The shirt fits you well. Which?
quizzes.takeaway: Me queda bien = it suits me. Me quedo = I stay.

quizzes.place: the end of almost any transaction
quizzes.question: The assistant finishes and says "ya está". What do they mean?
options: That is it, we are done
quizzes.answer: That is it, we are done
quizzes.takeaway: Ya está = done. You will hear it ten times a day.
